summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked). No values retrieved; all empirical items pending. Poverty baseline defined as the NLSS IV 2022/23 national-line headcount (NSO, Cost of Basic Needs, new line with 2022/23 base year per search-located NSO material, to confirm) with PIP international-line headcounts and Gini kept as a separate, differently constructed indicator (00B C-12): the two differ in poverty line, possibly welfare aggregate and spatial deflation, CPI/PPP conversion and PPP vintage, survey-year labelling, and PIP lined-up years are model extrapolations. NLSS III-IV comparison is not a like-for-like trend unless NSO back-casts. The NLSS IV data-quality critique flagged by 23C/10B is set up as a structured check list (sample frame, consumption module, survey/NA consumption ratio, census/BoP/NLFS consistency). Remittance income share is defined from the NLSS IV income-by-source module as both aggregate ratio and mean of household shares, by quintile/province, with an NRB BoP coverage diagnostic. Sixteen leads: ten search-located or shared (three of them, L02, L07, L08, with document identity to confirm), six general-knowledge URLs marked unverified.

findings.claim: Q1: Poverty headcount at the national poverty line (NLSS IV), national, urban/rural and by province, with standard errors.
findings.note: Required: NLSS IV poverty chapter tables (headcount, poverty gap, squared gap) and SEs; publication date. Leads: 14A-L01, 14A-L02, 14A-L03.

findings.claim: Q1: National poverty line value and its derivation (food line, non-food allowance, base year, spatial deflators).
findings.period: NLSS IV 2022/23 (per person per year, current NPR)
findings.note: Required: poverty-line annex of NLSS IV report: food basket, calorie norm, non-food allowance method, regional price indices. Leads: 14A-L01, 14A-L02.

findings.claim: Q1: Earlier-round national-line headcounts (NLSS I 1995/96, II 2003/04, III 2010/11) and whether NSO publishes an NLSS III estimate on the NLSS IV line.
findings.note: Required: NLSS III poverty report and any NSO back-cast; without a back-cast, the NLSS III-IV change is not a like-for-like trend. Leads: 14A-L13, 14A-L01.

findings.claim: Q1: International-line headcounts (PIP) at each current international poverty line for each Nepal survey in PIP, with PPP vintage, welfare type and survey/reporting year.
findings.period: PIP survey years (calendar-year labels) ; PPP vintage to record
findings.note: Required: PIP country profile/API extraction with retrieval date and PIP release version. Leads: 14A-L04, 14A-L05, 14A-L06.

findings.claim: Q1: International poverty line values in PIP (per person per day) and PPP vintage used.
findings.note: Required: PIP methodology note. Unit caveat: poverty lines are per person per day; units.py lacks a per-person-per-day PPP code (challenge to 01C) - store with explicit note until added. Leads: 14A-L06, 14A-L10.

findings.claim: Q1: PIP lined-up (nowcast) headcount for years after 2022/23.
findings.note: Required: PIP lined-up series flagged as extrapolated; treated as model estimate, never as survey fact. Leads: 14A-L04, 14A-L05.

findings.claim: Q2: Share of remittances in total household income (aggregate ratio and mean of household shares), national, urban/rural, province and consumption quintile; foreign and domestic remittances separately.
findings.note: Required: NLSS IV income-by-source tables or microdata income module with weights. Leads: 14A-L01, 14A-L03.

findings.claim: Q2: Share of households receiving remittances (any source; foreign only) by quintile and province.
findings.note: Required: NLSS IV remittance chapter; same observation set as 23C (no double ingestion). Leads: 14A-L01, 14A-L03.

findings.claim: Q2: Ratio of NLSS IV grossed-up foreign remittance receipts to NRB BoP personal remittances for FY2022/23 (survey coverage check).
findings.note: Required: NLSS IV total weighted remittance receipts and NRB FY2022/23 BoP inflow (23C observation). Different concepts; used only as coverage diagnostic. Leads: 14A-L01, 14A-L03.

findings.claim: Q3: Consumption Gini (per-capita, spatially deflated) from NLSS IV report.
findings.note: Required: NLSS IV inequality table; record scale (0-1 or 0-100) as published. Leads: 14A-L01, 14A-L03.

findings.claim: Q3: PIP Gini for Nepal by survey year and WDI SI.POV.GINI cross-check.
findings.note: Required: PIP/WDI extraction; differences vs NSO Gini to be explained by aggregate/deflator choice (C-12). Leads: 14A-L04, 14A-L05, 14A-L09.

findings.claim: Q3: Consumption shares by quintile/decile and Palma ratio (NLSS IV).
findings.note: Required: consumption distribution table or microdata. Leads: 14A-L01, 14A-L03.

findings.claim: Method: national-line and PIP headcounts are different indicators (different lines, possibly different welfare aggregates/deflators, PPP conversion, year labelling) and are reported side by side, never merged or averaged (C-12).

Method: the NSO adopted a new national poverty line with 2022/23 as base year (per search-located NSO material; to confirm on retrieval). Unless NSO publishes NLSS III on the new line, NLSS III and NLSS IV national-line headcounts are not a like-for-like trend.

Method: NLSS IV fieldwork falls within FY2022/23 (mid-July to mid-July) spanning two calendar years; PIP assigns its own survey-year label. Year labels are recorded as published and mapped only with a documented rule.

assumptions.text: The official welfare-dashboard poverty indicator is the NSO national-line headcount from the latest NLSS round; PIP is a comparison indicator.
Households are ranked by per-capita (spatially deflated) consumption for quintile analysis of remittance shares.
PIP lined-up estimates for non-survey years are model estimates and are labelled estimate, never fact, when ingested.
Remittance income share uses the NLSS IV definition of total household income; no re-imputation of missing income components in r2.

challenges.text: C-12 accepted. Add classifications 'survey-round comparability (national line rebased to 2022/23)' and 'lined-up extrapolation'. Escalation route for NLSS IV data-quality divergences.

units.py has no per-person-per-day PPP code; international poverty lines cannot be stored in native unit. Request e.g. PPP_const2021_per_person_day via Agent 00 (same issue as 10B's SDG 8.2.1 request).

Agree one NLSS IV observation set for remittance receipt; 14A adds income-share and quintile tabulations. Please record foreign vs within-Nepal remittances separately so 14A shares are not inflated by domestic transfers.
Social-transfer receipt and remittance income come from the same NLSS IV income module; share one extraction and one income definition.
Need household final consumption expenditure (NA) for FY2010/11 and FY2022/23 on a consistent vintage for the survey/NA consumption ratio check on NLSS IV.
Provincial poverty and gender breakdowns should use the 14A NLSS IV observation set and SEs; do not rank provinces where confidence intervals overlap.

uncertainty: Total for r1: no values retrieved. Main uncertainties for r2: (1) national vs PIP headcounts can diverge substantially for definitional and PPP-vintage reasons, so the gap itself is not evidence of error; (2) NLSS III-IV trend is not identified without an NSO back-cast; (3) NLSS IV data-quality critique unassessed; (4) survey income, especially remittances, is prone to under-reporting, so the remittance income share is likely a lower bound relative to BoP-based ratios, direction and size unknown until the coverage ratio is computed; (5) search-located documents L02, L07, L08 have unconfirmed identity.

dimensions.national: Cost of Basic Needs: food line from a reference basket priced at local prices meeting a calorie norm, plus non-food allowance; new line with 2022/23 base year (to confirm details)
dimensions.pip: International lines derived from national lines of poor countries, expressed in PPP dollars per person per day; line values change with PPP vintage

dimensions.national: Per-capita household consumption (food incl. own production, non-food, use value of durables, imputed/actual rent - components to confirm from NLSS IV annex)
dimensions.pip: PIP uses the survey's welfare aggregate (consumption for Nepal expected) as harmonised by World Bank; whether identical to the NSO aggregate is to be confirmed

dimensions.national: Spatial price deflators across survey domains/regions; line set in 2022/23 prices
dimensions.pip: CPI deflation from survey period to ICP base year, then PPP conversion (private consumption PPP); may or may not apply NSO spatial deflators
Headcount depends on PPP vintage (2017 vs 2021 ICP); record vintage and PIP release with each value

dimensions.national: NLSS I 1995/96, II 2003/04, III 2010/11, IV 2022/23; each round's line and aggregate differ; comparability requires NSO back-cast
dimensions.pip: Nepal surveys included in PIP and their year labels to be confirmed; lined-up years are interpolated/extrapolated with national-accounts growth (model estimates)

dimensions.status: method rule: record as published; no silent mapping

checks_planned: Read the critique (L11) and list each specific allegation before judging it
Sample frame and design (census frame used, strata, households, response) from microdata documentation
Consumption module design and recall periods vs NLSS III
Ratio of survey mean consumption to national-accounts household final consumption, NLSS III vs IV (NA from 01A observations)
Consistency of remittance incidence with census 2021 absentee households (10C) and NRB BoP (23C)
Consistency of labour indicators with NLFS (10B)
World Bank/PIP treatment: whether NLSS IV is accepted into PIP and any comparability flags
nlss_iv_data_quality_debate.escalation: If NSO and PIP (or survey vs NA benchmarks) diverge beyond tolerance with unclear cause, escalate to 00B.

metrics.definition: sum over households (weighted) of remittance receipts / sum of total household income
weighted mean of household-level remittance/income ratios
robustness check because survey income is typically less reliable than consumption

breakdowns: source (India / other countries / by country from microdata)
remittance_income_share.method: Use NLSS IV income-by-source module (the survey's own total-income definition, incl. imputed agricultural own-consumption if NSO includes it). Report aggregate share and mean-of-shares separately; rank households by per-capita consumption not income. Coverage diagnostic against NRB BoP FY2022/23 (23C) is a separate-concept comparison, not a calibration. Shared NLSS IV observation set with 23C/10B.
